# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am Deaf: I see everything on the bomb, I hear nothing. Looking at who can actually reach whom: Mute can hear AND see, so Mute is the only one I can have a two-way channel with (they gesture, I answer aloud — my voice reaches both of them). Blind can only ever be reached by my voice; Blind's voice never reaches me at all, only Mute. So I am the bridge: Mute's manual knowledge must flow through my mouth to Blind, and Blind's gestures are the only way Blind talks to me.

Mute opened with six gesture messages to me — [🤚 ✍], [✌ 👍], [👇 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝], [✋ ✌ 🤙], [✋ 👇 ☝], [🙏 👋]. I can't be certain of each one, but the themes look like: "tell/write what you see", "two — yes?" (the keypad wants two digits), possibly probing the display ("nine?" — it is 8, not 9), and a plea for any reply. Rather than guess symbol-by-symbol, the strongest answer is a complete spoken inventory: Mute hears it and can match it against the manual, and Blind gets it in the same breath, which Blind desperately needs since no one else can ever speak to Blind.

What I see: display 8, light yellow, strip red-red-blue, keypad buttons 9/7/8/1 wanting a two-digit code with nothing entered, six wires red/orange/yellow/green/white/blue. I'll send it to each separately so each knows who's talking, include a protocol note for Blind (gesture to me, never speak to me — I won't hear it), and confirm to Mute that the two-digit reading is right, plus a thumbs-up so they know the visual channel works.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Deaf. I hear nothing, but I saw all six of your gestures, and you can hear me, so I answer aloud. Full inventory of the bomb: the display reads 8. The light is yellow. The strip is painted in three segments, left to right: red, red, blue. The keypad has four buttons: position 1 shows 9, position 2 shows 7, position 3 shows 8, position 4 shows 1. It asks for a two-digit code and nothing is entered yet. There are six wires, left to right: red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. That is every colour, mark and reading on it. From now on: question me in gestures, I answer in words. Answering your signs: yes, two digits are wanted, and the display is 8, not 9.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am Deaf. I see the bomb, but I can never hear you, not even your voice; only Mute hears what you say. If you need to reach me, use gestures: I see every symbol you send. So your hands know the ground: on top, a display showing 8. Below it, a light glowing yellow. A strip painted in three segments: red, red, then blue rightmost. A keypad with four buttons showing 9, 7, 8 and 1, wanting a two-digit code, nothing entered yet. Six wires, left to right: red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Mute holds the manual and will route rules to you through my voice. Until then, feel all you like, but cut or press nothing.")

Meanwhile my three questions came back in order: procedure not yet delivered, nothing depends on my sight, defused once done.

Mute's repeating messages suddenly fit if trailing ☝-counts carry numbers: [✋ 👇 ☝ ☝×9] and [👇 ☝×9] = "press 9"; [✋ 👇 ☝] alone = "press 1"; [✌ 👍 ☝×4] = "second digit: the digit on button 4" = 1; [✋ ✌ 🤙 ☝×6] = "wire 6". Two independent readings converge: code 9 then 1 (leftmost button, then rightmost), wire 6 from the left (blue). I'll put that to Mute as ordered yes/no confirmations, with a pure counting fallback if anything is wrong, and canonize [🤚 ✍] as "there is more to tell". Blind gets the plan early to rehearse by position — with a strict hold until I say GO, since nothing is confirmed yet.
